assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative empirical programme that made intergenerational mobility measurable at population scale and reshaped analysis of opportunity and place.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked administrative-data mobility research programme.
assessment.maturity: The central measures, findings and policy relevance are well established across a substantial body of work.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit with other collaborators, including Lawrence F. Katz, requires careful resolution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work provided a highly influential account of how technology, tasks and trade shocks reshape labour demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson have distinct but strongly complementary contributions to the evidence and framework.
assessment.maturity: Its empirical influence and relevance to labour-market policy have accumulated over many years.
uncertainties: The broad discovery combines several mechanisms whose relative quantitative importance remains debated.
Lawrence F. Katz is an important potential claimant to credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony has changed how economists understand wage setting, employer power and labour-market institutions.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied a foundational framework, while Naidu is central to the modern empirical and policy-oriented development.
assessment.maturity: The topic has become a durable core of labour economics with growing empirical support.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping spans theoretical and empirical strands, making a limited attribution difficult.
Orley C. Ashenfelter's appropriate place in the credit requires scrutiny.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel methods and GMM became indispensable tools for credible empirical work with longitudinal data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond are closely and clearly associated with the core methodological advances.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been tested, extended and used across fields for decades.
uncertainties: The prize significance of a widely used econometric toolkit relative to broader conceptual discoveries is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of insurance theory with credible measurement of selection substantially advanced understanding of insurance markets and regulation.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are major contributors to the modern empirical literature connecting theory and market evidence.
assessment.maturity: A large subsequent literature supports the programme's importance and its policy consequences.
uncertainties: Bernard Salanie's precise share of credit and the boundaries of the discovery need fuller evaluation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification fundamentally clarified what data can establish under credible, limited assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the principal foundational figure in the discovery as framed.
assessment.maturity: The approach is longstanding, intellectually coherent and influential in econometrics and applied policy analysis.
uncertainties: Elie Tamer and Francesca Molinari made important contributions, but their relationship to a prize-sized shared attribution needs assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on teacher quality, educational production and accountability has materially changed education-policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Hanushek are prominent contributors to influential, complementary strands of the field.
assessment.maturity: The questions and evidence have persisted over decades and remain central to policy.
uncertainties: Evidence on particular accountability interventions is heterogeneous.
The candidate's broad framing makes exclusive attribution among all credited scholars difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This programme linked early-life environments, health and skill formation to long-run economic outcomes, with major implications for social policy.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Cunha are central contributors to empirical and dynamic human-capital strands respectively.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda is mature and supported by extensive work across settings.
uncertainties: The causal channels and the degree to which results generalize across contexts remain uncertain.
Douglas Almond's appropriate share of credit requires careful evaluation.
